title: Why Soda Cans Get Narrower At The Top

scenes.narration: The top of a soda can is visibly narrower than the rest of it, tapering inward just before the lid.
scenes.note: Make the taper visible — most people have never consciously seen it.

beats.action: a can stands in profile; the shoulder tapers in toward the lid
dimension lines measure body width against lid width
the taper highlights teal along the shoulder

scenes.narration: That taper is not shaped for your mouth.
scenes.note: Kill the intuitive wrong answer in one beat.

beats.action: a FOR YOUR MOUTH label appears and crosses out
the can rotates so the taper reads against the lid rim
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.narration: The lid has to be much thicker than the walls, because it holds the pressure and carries a tab you can tear open with one finger.
scenes.note: The asymmetry is the mechanism: lid metal is much thicker than wall metal. Show the gauge difference plainly.

beats.action: the can sections; wall and lid thickness draw at true relative scale
the lid gauge highlights, several times the wall gauge
internal pressure arrows push outward against the lid
a finger levers the tab; the lid flexes but holds

scenes.narration: Thick metal is expensive metal, so shrinking the lid saves far more aluminum than shaving the sides ever could.
scenes.note: The comparison that justifies the design: shrink the lid, not the walls.

beats.action: two strategies draw side by side — thinner walls, or a smaller lid
the lid shrinks; a large metal saving bar fills
the wall-shaving option barely moves its bar and is crossed out

scenes.narration: Six millimeters have come off it since the sixties, saving close to two hundred million pounds a year.
scenes.note: SCALE IS THE PAYOFF. Six millimetres, then multiply until the number is absurd. Hard cut.

beats.action: a 6 mm dimension line draws across the lid rim — almost nothing
the tiny measurement holds alone on screen
cans multiply across the frame until they fill it; a vast annual figure stamps; hard cut
the cans keep multiplying outward past the frame
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap
